operative_context: System shall maintain user identifier for each audit event
exceptions: Directly identifiable personal details may be restricted in raw logs if identity resolution is available through controlled access
conflicts_or_obsolete: Current compliance direction discourages exposing directly identifiable personal details in raw logs, conflicting with direct human-readable audit identity requirement
notes: R81b targets human-readable audit identity. PRIMARY evidence E1 establishes user account registration with mandatory user information (first name, last name, email). CONTEXT evidence E2 requires timestamp and user identifier logging (2.8.3). E5 and E6 reveal a tension: audit views currently use privacy-preserving identifiers that make operational review harder for non-technical auditors, and there is uncertainty about whether authorized reviewers should have controlled identity-resolution access. E7 confirms user identifier inclusion in reports (7.1.2). The core operative rule is that audit records must include user-linked traceability and be accessible to authorized reviewers in human-readable form. However, a significant gap exists between the requirement for human-readable identity and the current compliance direction that discourages exposing directly identifiable personal details in raw logs. The resolution mechanism (direct vs. controlled lookup) is unspecified. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: Audit records shall include user-linked traceability | Audit identity must be accessible to authorized reviewers | Human-readable audit identity should support operational review by non-technical auditors
